Narrative: UGT-22 is a membrane UDP-glycosyltransferase (Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=30.3); changes in glycosylation of secreted or membrane proteins could alter signaling milieu around AMso cells, but the connection to AMso asymmetric division is speculative without functional data.
rationale: UGT-22 is a membrane UDP-glycosyltransferase; while biochemical changes could influence signaling molecules, there is little direct evidence linking it to AMso fate specification.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable RNA binding activity. Predicted to be involved in regulatory ncRNA-mediated heterochromatin formation. Predicted to be located in nucleus and perinuclear region of cytoplasm. Predicted to be part of nuclear RNA-directed RNA polymerase complex. Expressed in Psub1; Psub2; Psub3; Psub4; and germ cell. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in immunodeficiency 91. Is an ortholog of human ZNFX1 (zinc finger NFX1-type containing 1).
Narrative: ZK1067.2 is predicted to bind RNA and participate in nuclear RNA-directed RNA polymerase complexes (Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=35.4); disruption could perturb regulatory ncRNA pathways and indirectly affect gene expression programs during AMso division, but evidence is indirect and mainly germline-associated.
rationale: ZK1067.2 is predicted RNA-binding and part of nuclear RNA-directed RNA polymerase complex expressed in germ cells; potential regulatory roles are distant from AMso-specific asymmetric divisions.

WB_Overview: Predicted to be located in membrane.
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: lact-2 encodes a beta-lactamase domain-containing protein that contains a predicted transmembrane domain in its N terminus.
Narrative: LACT-2 is a transmembrane beta-lactamase-domain protein (Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=20.3); alterations could influence membrane-associated signaling or processing of extracellular signals relevant to AMso cells, but the gene lacks known roles in neuronal fate decisions making it a low-probability candidate.
rationale: LACT-2 is a membrane beta-lactamase-domain protein; a missense could affect membrane-associated processes but lacks direct links to neuronal fate or asymmetric division.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable calcium ion binding activity. Predicted to be involved in cell-cell adhesion. Predicted to be located in membrane. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in Van Maldergem syndrome 1 and mitral valve prolapse. Is an ortholog of human DCHS1 (dachsous cadherin-related 1).
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: cdh-1 encodes a cadherin that is similar, in the extracellular domain, to the Drosophila cadherin Dachsous (Ds); although the precise role of cdh-1 in C. elegans development and/or behavior is not yet known, loss of cdh-1 activity via RNAi using the hypersensitive rrf-3 strain can result in locomotion and growth defects, as well as larval lethality.
pubmed_ref_avaiable: PMID 15924262: APC/C regulation of axonal growth and synaptic functions in postmitotic neurons: the Liprin-alpha connection. (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15924262/)
agent1_publication_comments: PMID15924262: Irrelevant - score:3 Reason:The summary shows Cdh-1/APC/C functions in postmitotic neurons modulating axonal growth and synaptic function via Liprin-α, but it does not describe roles in asymmetric division, lineage-specific fate decisions, or glial-to-neuronal transdifferentiation of the AMso->MCM lineage. Thus it lacks a direct mechanistic link to the specific MCM loss phenotype driven by a symmetric AMso division.
Narrative: CDH-1 is a cadherin predicted to mediate cell-cell adhesion (Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=31.3); altered adhesion could change AMso daughter positioning or local cell interactions that feed into fate decisions, offering a plausible but indirect mechanism for MCM loss.
rationale: CDH-1 is a cadherin predicted to mediate cell-cell adhesion; altered adhesion could perturb local positioning or signaling of AMso daughters but direct evidence is limited.

WB_Overview: Predicted to be located in membrane. Expressed in virL and virR.
Narrative: F55G1.6 is a membrane protein with limited annotation (Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=28.6); absent functional links to neuronal fate or asymmetric division make this a low-confidence candidate for causing MCM loss without follow-up data.
rationale: F55G1.6 is membrane-localized with limited annotation; a missense is unlikely to specifically explain MCM loss without additional functional data.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable acyltransferase activity, transferring groups other than amino-acyl groups. Predicted to be involved in polysaccharide biosynthetic process. Predicted to be located in membrane.
Narrative: OAC-19 is an acyltransferase predicted to be membrane-localized (Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=8.1); while membrane lipid modification can affect signaling, there is no direct evidence linking OAC-19 to AMso asymmetric division or neuronal specification, so causal probability is low.
rationale: OAC-19 is a predicted acyltransferase with no clear role in neuronal fate decisions or asymmetric division, making it a low-probability candidate for MCM-specific loss.
